original_question: Let (X, H) be a smooth complex projective polarized variety. Does there always exist a class gamma in the numerical Chow ring of the form gamma = e^{-B} * (1, 0, Gamma, gamma_3, ..., gamma_n) together with an upper semicontinuous function f^gamma: R -> R such that every gamma-tilt-semistable object E satisfies the quadratic inequality Q_{s,q}(E) >= 0 for all (s, q) in Delta with q > f^gamma(s)?
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, Conjecture 5.13 (Bayer–Macrì), which the survey explicitly identifies as [10, Conjecture 4.7].
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main content of the statement: it is about a smooth complex projective polarized variety (X,H), the existence of a class gamma in the numerical Chow ring of the form e^{-B}·(1,0,Gamma,gamma_3,...,gamma_n), an upper semicontinuous function f^gamma: R -> R, and a universal quadratic inequality Q_{s,q}(E) >= 0 for gamma-tilt-semistable objects in a region Delta. It also correctly captures that the conjecture is existential and is meant to hold uniformly over all relevant stability parameters.
missing_details: The paper’s exact target is Conjecture 5.13 in Section 5.3, not a broader informal question; it is introduced only after the survey defines ordinary tilt-stability and explains that the naive generalized Bogomolov inequality fails in general.

The class gamma is not arbitrary: the nearby context specifies B in NS(X) tensor R, Gamma in CH^2_num(X) tensor R with Gamma·H^{n-2} = 0, and gamma_i in CH^i_num(X) tensor R for 3 <= i <= n, with gamma := e^{-B}·(1,0,Gamma,gamma_3,...,gamma_n).

The semistability condition is parameter-dependent: the conjecture quantifies over objects E that are sigma^gamma_{s,q}-semistable for the same pair (s,q), not just over objects that are 'gamma-tilt-semistable' in some unspecified sense.
The region Delta must be defined explicitly as Delta = {(s,q) in R^2 : q > s^2/2}.
The conjecture is about objects E in D^b(X), not only coherent sheaves or an unspecified class of objects.

To make the question stand-alone, one should define the modified Chern character ch^gamma(-) := gamma·ch(-), the vector v_H^gamma(E) = (H^n ch_0^gamma(E), H^{n-1} ch_1^gamma(E), ..., H·ch_{n-1}^gamma(E), ch_n^gamma(E)), and the notation v_i^gamma for its components.
The quadratic form Q_{s,q}(E) should be defined explicitly rather than left implicit.

No extra nilpotency hypothesis is stated in the paper beyond working in the graded numerical Chow ring CH^bullet_num(X) tensor R; if one wants the question to be fully self-contained, that should be left implicit only if the graded-ring interpretation of e^{-B} is understood.
refined_question:
Let (X,H) be a smooth complex projective polarized variety of dimension n. Is it true that there exist classes B in NS(X) tensor R, Gamma in CH^2_num(X) tensor R with Gamma·H^{n-2} = 0, and gamma_i in CH^i_num(X) tensor R for 3 <= i <= n, defining

gamma := e^{-B}·(1,0,Gamma,gamma_3,...,gamma_n) in CH^bullet_num(X) tensor R,

and an upper semicontinuous function f^gamma: R -> R, such that for every (s,q) in Delta := {(s,q) in R^2 : q > s^2/2} and every object E in D^b(X) that is sigma^gamma_{s,q}-semistable, one has Q_{s,q}(E) >= 0 whenever q > f^gamma(s), where ch^gamma(-) := gamma·ch(-), v_H^gamma(E) := (H^n ch_0^gamma(E), H^{n-1} ch_1^gamma(E), ..., H·ch_{n-1}^gamma(E), ch_n^gamma(E)), and Q_{s,q}(E) is the Bayer–Macrì quadratic form built from the first four components v_0^gamma, v_1^gamma, v_2^gamma, v_3^gamma?
justification: The draft is aiming at the revised generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture stated in the survey as Conjecture 5.13, not at a different Torelli-type question. Section 5.3 first defines the ordinary tilt-stability family sigma_{s,q} and the parameter region Delta in Theorem 5.11, then explains why the older inequality is too optimistic, and finally introduces the modified class gamma, the modified Chern character ch^gamma, and the exact conjectural statement. The survey explicitly says that Conjecture 5.13 is [10, Conjecture 4.7], so this is the nearest official formulation in arXiv:2201.03899 itself. Your draft is mathematically close, but it omits several paper-critical definitions: the condition Gamma·H^{n-2}=0, the fact that semistability depends on the same pair (s,q), the definition of Delta, the ambient category D^b(X), and the auxiliary definitions needed to make Q_{s,q}(E) meaningful as a stand-alone question.
